question: Should OpenClaw consolidate memory management around a new public memory mode/config/API now, and should the open memory role-slot PR be the canonical implementation path for that direction?
rationale: Current main still has multiple memory mechanisms and single-slot plugin ownership, while the requested fix changes durable public config, plugin API, storage, docs, and migration behavior that automation should not choose on its own.

options.title: Review role-slot PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as the main implementation review path, then keep or narrow this issue for remaining memory UX/storage consistency after that decision.

options.title: Narrow to docs and doctor UX first
options.body: Defer new memory API surface and instead make current builtin/QMD/plugin behavior more discoverable, diagnosable, and migratable before changing config semantics.

options.title: Reject core memory reshaping
options.body: Close this direction only if maintainers decide current plugin/backend seams are sufficient and memory composition should stay outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Review role-slot PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as the main implementation review path, then keep or narrow this issue for remaining memory UX/storage consistency after that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public config/plugin API and memory product-direction decision, and steipete has the strongest current history on the reviewed runtime/config surfaces.
